# Manual case: does DXIL container signing actually happen, and does dxil.dll matter?

The issue is titled "Problem with DXIL signing", and the reported output carries
`warning: DXIL.dll not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed for use in release
environments.`  Signing is not something `cmd.txt` can measure, so it is measured here by
hand: compile, write a container with `-Fo`, and read the 16-byte digest at offset 4 of the
`DXBC` header (`DxilContainerHeader::Hash`, hashed from `offsetof(..., Version)` to the end
by `ComputeHashRetail` -- `lib/DxilContainer/DxcContainerBuilder.cpp:185-204`,
`tools/clang/tools/dxcvalidator/dxcvalidator.cpp:36-52`).

Shell: PowerShell 7.  `$GT` = `C:\prj\DirectXShaderCompiler\build\Debug\bin\dxc.exe`
(ground truth, `1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907)`).  Run from this directory.  `.dxo` outputs
are scratch and were deleted after the digests below were read; re-running the commands
regenerates them.

`control-default-case.hlsl` is used for every signing probe because the *repro* fails
validation and therefore produces no container at all -- which is itself the first result.

---

## 1. Ground truth, default environment

```
$ $GT -T ps_6_0 -E MainPS control-default-case.hlsl -Fo sign-probe-gt.dxo
exit=0
magic=DXBC
hash=787986802743ecdd403360764860bb71
```

Non-zero digest: **the container is hashed/signed with no `dxil.dll` involved at all.**

## 2. Ground truth, external validator forced on

`dxil.dll` *is* present next to the ground-truth `dxc.exe` (10,720,768 bytes,
`FileVersion 1.9.0.5393`, `damyanp/fix-resource-struct-zero-init, dc2088b20-dirty`,
Authenticode `NotSigned` -- a local build, not the retail DLL).  It is **not loaded by
default**: since PR #7451 (`NFC: remove dead external validation code paths from
dxcompiler`) `dxcompiler.dll` no longer probes for a sibling `dxil.dll`; `dxc.exe` loads one
only when `DXC_DXIL_DLL_PATH` names an absolute path
(`lib/DxcSupport/dxcapi.extval.cpp:433-462`).

```
$ $env:DXC_DXIL_DLL_PATH='C:\prj\DirectXShaderCompiler\build\Debug\bin\dxil.dll'
$ $GT --version
dxcompiler.dll: 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433) - 1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907); C:\prj\DirectXShaderCompiler\build\Debug\bin\dxil.dll: 1.10 - 1.9.0.5393 (damyanp/fix-resource-struct-zero-init, dc2088b20-dirty)

$ $GT -T ps_6_0 -E MainPS control-default-case.hlsl -Fo sign-probe-ext.dxo
exit=0
hash=787986802743ecdd403360764860bb71        <-- byte-identical to case 1
```

**The external validator produces the same signature as the internal one.**  Signing is not
contingent on `dxil.dll` on a current build.

## 3. Ground truth, external validator forced on, running the repro

```
$ $GT -T ps_6_0 -E MainPS repro.hlsl
error: validation errors

Function: MainPS: error: Instructions must be of an allowed type.
note: at 'unreachable' in block '#4' of function 'MainPS'.
Validation failed.
exit=-2136342519   (0x80AA0009, DXC_E_IR_VERIFICATION_FAILED)
```

Same rule, same defect -- but two differences from the default configuration
(`out-main-debug.txt`, which exits `0x80004005`):

* the **exit code changes** from `E_FAIL` to `0x80AA0009`.  Neither is an internal failure
  (severity nibble 8), so `is_internal_failure` classifies both correctly, but a predicate
  keyed to a specific non-zero exit code would have been wrong under one of them;
* the **source location is lost**: `Function: MainPS:` replaces `repro.hlsl:24:1:`.

The reproduction itself is unaffected, which is the point of the probe.

## 4. `dxil.dll` across every release probed

`out-*.txt` for all 20 releases: **no probe printed `DXIL.dll not found`**.  The string is
present in the v1.4.1907 binary (verified by scanning `dxcompiler.dll` for it), so its
absence from the output means the DLL was found and loaded, not that the warning was
unavailable.  The string is present in every `dxcompiler.dll` from v1.4.1907 through
v1.8.2407 and absent from v1.8.2505 onward.

`dxc --version` gives the same answer directly, for the releases that support the flag
(v1.4.1907-v1.6.2106 answer `Unknown argument: '--version'`):

| release | `--version` reports |
| --- | --- |
| v1.7.2207 | `dxcompiler.dll: 1.7 - 1.7.2207.3 (e9137cd1d); dxil.dll: 1.7(101.7.2207.10)` |
| v1.7.2212 | `... ; dxil.dll: 1.7(101.7.2212.14)` |
| v1.7.2212.1 | `... ; dxil.dll: 1.7(101.7.2212.36)` |
| v1.8.2403 | `... ; dxil.dll: 1.8(101.8.2403.18)` |
| v1.8.2403.1 | `... ; dxil.dll: 1.8(101.8.2403.21)` |
| v1.8.2403.2 | `... ; dxil.dll: 1.8(101.8.2403.24)` |
| v1.8.2405 | `... ; dxil.dll: 1.8(101.8.2405.17)` |
| v1.8.2407 | `... ; dxil.dll: 1.8(101.8.2407.12)` |
| v1.8.2505 | `dxcompiler.dll: 1.9 - 1.8.2505.28 (9efbb6c32); dxil.dll: 1.9(1.8.2505.28)` |
| v1.9.2602 | `dxcompiler.dll: 1.9(5184-21d28f72)(1.9.2602.17) - 1.9.2602.17 (21d28f727)` -- **no dxil.dll** |
| v1.9.2602.24 | no `dxil.dll` |
| v1.9.2607 | no `dxil.dll` |
| main-debug | no `dxil.dll` |

Every release tree in the cache *ships* a `dxil.dll` next to its `dxc.exe` (checked with
`Get-AuthenticodeSignature`: v1.4.1907 carries the SDK's `10.0.18362.1`, `Valid`;
v1.5.2010 `NotSigned`; v1.6.2104/2106 `UnknownError`; every release from v1.7.2207 `Valid`),
so no probe in this issue ran without a validator available.  What changes across the range
is whether DXC *uses* it: auto-loaded through v1.8.2505, ignored from v1.9.2602 on.

That split is real but does not affect this verdict: all 21 probes fail on the same
validator rule and exit `0x80004005`.

## 5. `-Vd`, and what disabling validation removes

`variant-vd-novalidation-main-debug.txt` -- `-T ps_6_0 -E MainPS -Vd repro.hlsl`, exit 0.
The compile succeeds and emits the module the validator was rejecting:

```llvm
  switch i32 %4, label %17 [
    i32 0, label %5
    i32 1, label %9
    i32 2, label %13
  ]
...
; <label>:17                                      ; preds = %0
  unreachable
```

This is @tristanlabelle's 2019 diagnosis, confirmed: the fall-off-the-end path becomes an
LLVM `unreachable`, which is not a legal DXIL instruction.

`-Vd` is not a workaround for this issue: it does not just skip the diagnostic, it also
**leaves the container unsigned**, which is the very thing the issue title is about.
Measured digests, same 16 bytes at offset 4, same shader unless stated:

| compiler | input | flags | digest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main-debug | `control-default-case.hlsl` | (none) | `787986802743ecdd403360764860bb71` |
| main-debug | `control-default-case.hlsl` | `DXC_DXIL_DLL_PATH` set | `787986802743ecdd403360764860bb71` |
| main-debug | `control-default-case.hlsl` | `-Vd` | `00000000000000000000000000000000` |
| main-debug | `repro.hlsl` | `-Vd` | `00000000000000000000000000000000` |
| v1.4.1907 | `control-default-case.hlsl` | (none) | `92c0940d85b841f27b958aa403b824d8` |
| v1.9.2607 | `control-default-case.hlsl` | (none) | `27f119687e6ad9ca88bbdc7de5072ed0` |

So: a validated compile is signed on the oldest and newest releases and on ground truth,
with or without an external `dxil.dll`; `-Vd` is the only configuration measured here that
produces an all-zero (unsigned) digest.  The two release digests differ from each other only
because the DXIL they cover differs between compiler versions.

`-Vd` appears nowhere in the issue and is **not** in `cmd.txt`.
